topic: Classifying Materials by Absorbency, Buoyancy, and Decay
key_concepts: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
Matter exists as solid, liquid, and gas.
Solids can be classified by properties such as size, shape, color, texture, weight, and wa
Porous materials have small holes that allow air or liquid to pass through; non-porous mat
Cotton is very porous and absorbs water well.
Objects float if they are less dense than the liquid and sink if they are denser.
Buoyancy is the tendency of an object to float in a liquid.
Some objects float at first and later sink as they absorb water.
Decay is the slow breakdown of materials in the presence of water, air, and soil.
Decomposers break down organic materials and return nutrients to the ecosystem.
Factors such as sunlight, water, soil, and microorganisms contribute to decay.
